entries.title: Sage 300 People MCS service cannot start after a password change
entries.likelyCause: The Windows or SQL account used by the MCS service has a new or expired password, so the stored credentials no longer authenticate.
steps: Confirm the account used by the MCS service and whether its password changed or expired.
Update the credentials in the Sage 300 People configuration utility.
Restart the MCS service and confirm it starts under the correct account.

links.title: Sage Knowledgebase search: Sage 300 People MCS service

entries.title: ESS mobile registration fails with an invalid or expired QR code
entries.likelyCause: Registration codes are time limited and tied to the employee self-service user, so an expired code or an inactive ESS user blocks registration.
steps: Confirm the employee is active and linked to an enabled ESS user.
Generate a new registration QR code and use it immediately.
Confirm the device date, time and network access to the ESS URL.

links.title: Sage Knowledgebase search: Sage 300 People ESS mobile registration

entries.title: PAYE differs between two payroll periods
entries.likelyCause: PAYE is calculated on the annual equivalent, so once-off earnings, backdated payments, a changed tax status or outdated tax tables change the result between periods.
steps: Confirm the tax tables for the tax year were imported.
Compare taxable earnings, deductions and year-to-date values for both periods.
Check for once-off or backdated earnings that change the annual equivalent.
Recalculate in a copy of the database before changing live payroll data.

links.title: Sage Knowledgebase search: Sage 300 People PAYE calculation

entries.title: Bill of materials does not produce the expected batch yield
entries.likelyCause: The bill of materials build quantity and the component units of measure determine the yield, so a mismatch produces the wrong finished quantity or cost.
steps: Confirm the build quantity on the bill of materials and the units of measure of each component.
Create a test assembly for the required batch and compare the component usage.
Review the resulting I/C costing entries before posting in the live company.

links.title: Sage Knowledgebase search: Sage 300 bill of materials assembly

entries.title: Vendor or customer cannot be selected on a G/L control account
entries.likelyCause: Accounts flagged as subledger control accounts only accept postings created by A/P or A/R, so direct G/L journal entries are blocked by design.
steps: Confirm the control account flag on the G/L account.
Post the transaction through A/P or A/R instead.
Reconcile the control account to the subledger aged report.

links.title: Sage Knowledgebase search: Sage 300 G/L control account

entries.title: Bank reconciliation is out of balance after a statement import
entries.likelyCause: Duplicated or unmatched statement lines, or entries posted directly to the bank G/L account, leave the reconciliation out of balance.
steps: Confirm the statement opening and closing balances.
List unmatched and duplicated statement entries after the import.
Look for journals posted directly to the bank G/L account.

links.title: Sage Knowledgebase search: Sage 300 bank reconciliation out of balance

entries.title: Inventory costs are missing until Day End Processing runs
entries.likelyCause: Costing and audit records are only created by Day End Processing, so outstanding or failed Day End runs leave transactions without cost.
steps: Confirm when Day End Processing last completed.
Run Day End Processing in a test copy and capture any error.
Review the I/C costing and audit reports afterwards.

links.title: Sage Knowledgebase search: Sage 300 day end processing

entries.title: Third-party product compatibility with a Sage release
entries.likelyCause: Compatibility between Sage and an add-on is published by the add-on vendor, so it has to be confirmed against the vendor matrix rather than assumed.
steps: Record the exact Sage version, update level and the add-on version.
Check the vendor compatibility matrix for that combination.
Obtain written vendor confirmation before scheduling the upgrade.
